syntax: SELECT ... FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.key = b.foreign_key;
documentation: An inner join combines rows when the join condition is true. Rows with no match are omitted. Multiple matching rows produce multiple result rows.
inputs: Two related tables and a join condition.
caution: A missing or incorrect join condition can multiply rows unexpectedly. Qualify shared column names.
scenarios: Show customer names beside service jobs.
Connect invoice lines to product details.
Build a booking list with staff names.
title: Attach customers to jobs
problem: customers has id and name. jobs has id and customer_id. Return jobs.id AS job_id and customers.name AS customer_name for matched records only, ordered by job_id ascending.
goal: Use INNER JOIN or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Two jobs for one customer
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE jobs (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Micki'),(2,'Andrew'); INSERT INTO jobs VALUES (9,1),(7,2),(8,1);

tests.name: Unmatched job
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE jobs (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Ava'); INSERT INTO jobs VALUES (2,99);
